record.title: GEM reports that geometric coverage can miss task evidence in agent-history compression
record.summary: A September 2026 preprint introduces GEM, a training-free compressor that protects selected task and execution evidence before adding history blocks by geometric residual. In a matched-retained-count offline analysis, authors report next-action Top-3 block retention of 0.69 versus 0.31 for geometry-only selection across 650 checkpoints from 32 trajectories, while pooled centroid similarity rounds to 0.98 in both conditions. In a separate 260-task online benchmark, authors report 21.4% lower mean combined token use (2.69M to 2.11M per task) and reward of 70.18 versus 69.87. Results vary by domain; the offline metric is not task success, and the preprint has not been independently reproduced.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The preprint describes GEM, a training-free compressor that protects selected task and execution evidence, then adds history blocks by geometric residual; retained original blocks are forwarded in chronological order.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In a matched-retained-count analysis over 650 checkpoints from 32 trajectories, authors report next-action Top-3 history-block retention of 0.69 with evidence constraints versus 0.31 with geometry-only selection, while pooled centroid similarity rounds to 0.98 in both conditions. Authors treat trajectories as independent units and say the pooled means do not establish statistical equivalence.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across 260 WorkBuddyBench tasks, authors report mean combined token use falling from 2.69M to 2.11M per task and mean reward changing from 69.87 to 70.18; domain outcomes vary, including only a small token reduction and lower reward on Code tasks.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The offline Top-3 metric measures retention of blocks most similar to a recorded next action, not task success. The separate 20-task online ablation is small and mixed by domain; the fixed-40 baseline comparison uses a separate, unpaired panel.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the reported offline retention analyses or online benchmark outcomes has been completed.
Trajectory-level uncertainty estimates for the pooled matched-budget means and replication on another benchmark are needed to assess generality.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported results reproduce, they show that common geometric coverage measures can overlook history blocks tied to later agent actions, affecting how long-context systems are evaluated and compressed. The 260-task online result also bears on memory cost and task reward, but the evidence is from one author-run benchmark and does not establish universal savings or task success from the offline retention metric.
limitations: All performance measurements are author-reported and have not been independently reproduced.

The matched-budget comparison pools checkpoint means descriptively; the 32 trajectories, not 650 checkpoints, are the independent units, and reported centroid similarity does not establish statistical equivalence.
Next-action Top-3 retention is an offline representation metric, not agent task success.
The primary online result is one 260-task benchmark and hides domain variation; Code has little token reduction and lower mean reward.
The 20-task online ablation is small; the fixed-40 reference is a separate, unpaired panel.
brief.summary: A September 2026 preprint introduces GEM, a training-free compressor that protects selected task and execution evidence before adding history blocks by geometric residual. In a matched-retained-count offline analysis, authors report next-action Top-3 block retention of 0.69 versus 0.31 for geometry-only selection across 650 checkpoints from 32 trajectories, while pooled centroid similarity rounds to 0.98 in both conditions. In a separate 260-task online benchmark, authors report 21.4% lower mean combined token use (2.69M to 2.11M per task) and reward of 70.18 versus 69.87. Results vary by domain; the offline metric is not task success, and the preprint has not been independently reproduced.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report higher next-action Top-3 retention at matched block counts and lower combined token use with similar aggregate reward on WorkBuddyBench Full260. The 260-task mean hides variation: Code reward falls 1.74 points with little token reduction, while Security has the largest token decrease. A separate 20-task ablation reports 35.3% fewer combined tokens but a 0.36-point lower overall reward than base.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper counts model input, model output and embedding tokens together. It reports use of a frozen 1,024-dimensional Qwen3-Embedding-8B encoder and DeepSeek-V4-Flash at temperature zero for the main online evaluation. No independent cost audit was performed.
technical.demonstrated_result: The method, metric definitions, benchmark tables, controls, online ablation and appendix protocols are inspectable in the primary preprint. Performance outcomes remain CLAIMED as author-run results.
technical.implementation_status: Research preprint describing a training-free external compressor; no independent deployment or reproduction is established.
technical.mechanism: GEM keeps complete original interaction blocks, first protecting recent, goal-related, state, error and source evidence. It then fills a selected core using geometric residuals and forwards selected original messages in chronological order. A request-length deletion guard limits each rewrite to at most 5% of serialized characters; nominal core capacity is not a hard bound on forwarded blocks.
technical.novelty: Separates task and execution evidence protection from geometric coverage selection, and tests evidence retention independently of global representation similarity.
technical.regime: WorkBuddyBench Full260: 260 tasks across Code, Office, Security and Web, using DeepSeek-V4-Flash and frozen Qwen3-Embedding-8B representations. Matched-budget offline comparison: 650 checkpoints from 32 trajectories. Additional selector sweeps use 28 trajectories/525 checkpoints and 32 trajectories/59 checkpoints; online ablation uses 20 tasks.
technical.reproducibility: The primary preprint exposes definitions, settings, ablations and tables. No independent reproduction or code execution was performed in this activation. The 650-checkpoint means are pooled descriptively; trajectories are the independent units.
technical.strongest_baseline: Geometry-only selection is the matched-budget comparator for the 650-checkpoint evidence-retention result. Online reward/token comparisons include the base agent; the fixed-40 reference panel compares several memory and compression methods but is a separate unpaired task panel.

brief.title: GEM reports that geometric coverage can miss task evidence in agent-history compression
brief.why_it_matters: History compressors can preserve a global representation while discarding records that carry distinct execution evidence. GEM provides a concrete test of that distinction and reports lower aggregate token use on one online benchmark. Its offline evidence-retention measure must not be read as task success, and the author-run results need independent replication.
